note: Queries that do not resolve AS THE ROLE THEIR MODULE CONNECTS AS. See role_contract.mjs. Entries may only be REMOVED — never edited to hide a regression, and never added without a reason. A baselined site that starts passing fails the build, so this list can only shrink.
source: HP-RECON-004 — the request path has no role

entries.why: The ingestion job shares src/db/pool.ts, which is built from DATABASE_URL — i.e. hp_app, which holds USAGE on public only. dqe_role is the role with evidence and safety USAGE and is the one this job is designed around. Ten sites, one cause: the job has never been given its own pool.

entries.why: obs.ai_call INSERT is granted to redflag_role and to nothing else, but the request path logs COMPOSE and CATEGORY_CLASSIFY calls too, so moving anthropic.ts onto the red-flag pool would be the wrong shape. Needs obs.record_ai_call(...).
obs.fabrication_block has no INSERT grant to any application role. Needs obs.record_fabrication_block(...).
safety.safety_template SELECT is held by redflag_role. A pool change, not a migration: this module is only ever reached from the red-flag path.
safety.emergency_facility_reference SELECT is held by redflag_role. Pool change.
safety.emergency_contact_reference SELECT is held by redflag_role. Pool change.

The side-effect worker runs on the app's own DATABASE_URL, so it is hp_app, and it reads safety.clinician_alert — which hp_app cannot reach at all. It is also the consumer half of side_effect_job, the stub-invented queue R10b replaces with obs.review_queue_item.
